subject: Post-call: evidence pack specification & sample delivery
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Pruitt <alex.pruitt@greengrid.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: evidence pack specification & sample delivery

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can scope the evidence pack you requested: 

- What we heard: GreenGrid needs a downloadable proof bundle showing who accessed PII (email, device IDs) over the last 90 days, with timestamps, user role, source IP, and the query/endpoint hit.
- Key constraints you mentioned: exports must not include raw PII unless redacted; we should provide both redacted and tokenized identifier views. You also flagged that retention rules differ between EU and US projects.

Could you confirm the exact fields you need in the CSV export? Our suggested baseline (to confirm): timestamp (UTC), resource_id, resource_type, accessed_by (internal_id), role, action, source_ip, request_path, data_exposure_flag, redaction_level, retention_bucket.

Next steps from our side once you confirm schema:
1) We’ll generate a small sample CSV for your review (redwood-audit-sample.csv) and a PII-mapping template (pii-mapping-template.xlsx).
2) Rishi (security) will include the evidence chain (hashes, signature) and notes on redaction/derivatization.
3) Delivery options: secure S3 link + GDrive copy, or upload to your vendor portal — which do you prefer?

Also, is 90 days the correct retention window for this request or should we include 180-day samples as well (some teams ask for both)?

Thanks — I’ll pause on producing the full pack until you confirm the schema and delivery preference.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: export-spec-v1.pdf (PDF, 38 KB)]

From: Alex Pruitt <alex.pruitt@greengrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: GreenGrid Security <security@greengrid.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Dec 2025 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: evidence pack specification & sample delivery

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and very helpful list. Confirming:

- Fields: the baseline you listed works. Add an optional ‘session_id’ column if available.
- Redaction: we want two artifacts — 1) fully redacted CSV (no PII), 2) pseudonymized CSV where PII is replaced by stable tokens so we can correlate events across exports.
- Retention windows: start with 90 days, but please include an appendix with a 180-day sample (no need for full 180 days for every log type).
- Delivery: secure S3 link is preferred. Please set objects to expire per your retention policy but keep the sample available for 30 days.

One more ask from our side: can you include a short narrative or metadata file describing how redaction/pseudonymization was performed (hashing algorithm, salts, whether HSM was used for keys)? Security will also want an assertion that exports were generated from immutable audit store snapshots.

If you can send the sample CSV and mapping template tomorrow that would be great.

— Alex
Alex Pruitt
Security Lead, GreenGrid Energy

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Dec 2025 14:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: evidence pack specification & sample delivery

Marissa / team — attaching the initial artifacts and engineering notes. Key points: 

- Redaction vs pseudonymization: redaction removes PII fields. Pseudonymization replaces PII with deterministic HMAC-SHA256 tokens using a derivation key stored in KMS (no raw salts in export). The derivation is deterministic per-account so tokens are stable across exports for correlation.
- Immutable snapshot: logs are exported from our write-once audit ledger (ledger_id: L-9931); each export is accompanied by an SHA256 manifest and signed with our platform key. We will include the manifest (manifest-sha256.txt) with the sample.
- Export format: CSV UTF-8, comma-delimited, header row included. Timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC. For large exports we also provide gzipped NDJSON if preferred.

Attachments included: redwood-audit-sample.csv (redacted), redwood-audit-sample-pseudonymized.csv, pii-mapping-template.xlsx, manifest-sha256.txt.

Notes for Ben: use the engineering export job named 'evidence_pack_job_v3' and tag the S3 objects with: project=greengrid, deal_id=GG-2025-1497, retention=30d-sample. Let me know if you need help with the signed manifest step.

Rishi
Director, Security Engineering | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: manifest-sha256.txt (TXT, 1 KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Pruitt <alex.pruitt@greengrid.com>
Cc: GreenGrid Security <security@greengrid.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2025 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: evidence pack specification & sample delivery

Alex — thanks for the quick confirmation. We’ve uploaded the requested artifacts to a temporary S3 staging link (expires 2026-01-01):

- https://s3.redwood-example.com/staging/greengrid/GG-2025-1497/evidence-pack-samples/

Included in the folder: redwood-audit-sample.csv (redacted), redwood-audit-sample-pseudonymized.csv, pii-mapping-template.xlsx, manifest-sha256.txt, export-spec-v1.pdf, and the short narrative (redaction_pseudonymization_notes.txt) describing the algorithms and KMS usage. 

Summary of the evidence items:
- Redacted CSV: PII columns removed.
- Pseudonymized CSV: deterministic tokens generated via HMAC-SHA256 (KMS-backed key).
- Manifest: SHA256 of the exported file and signature.
- Delivery: objects are tagged per your request; sample retention on staging is 30 days.

Please confirm receipt and whether GreenGrid security wants a short walkthrough call to review the manifest/signature verification (Rishi is available). If all looks good we’ll prepare the 180-day appendix and provide a one-page attestation you can include in your compliance folder.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
